question: door-hardware-sets
unit: per door leaf (ea) — complete hardware set, supplied and fitted

band.unit: per door leaf (ea) — complete hardware set, supplied and fitted
band.centre: Auckland (AKL rates; WLG/CHC within ~3% on the QV rows used)
band.basis: Sum of nine distinct components, no double counting: lockset+lever furniture (QV t2:r5, 728–1040), overhead closer (QV t24:r2, 320–800), 3 hinges (QV t0:r11 x3, 117.60), floor door stop (QV t22:r4, 51), restricted-keyway cylinder (QV t7:r11 anchor, +20%/+140%, 60–120), installation labour (QV carpenter 81.30/hr x 1.5–2.0 hr, 122–163), registered key cutting (LockSmart 10–20/key x3, 30–60), bench keying to master system (LockSmart 60–100/lock x1, 60–100) and the amortised master-key/handover allowance (8–20). Total for the nominal 25 leaves $37,425–$61,800, excl. GST. Allowances are ~5% of the total, so the band does not rest on them. Low confidence is driven by two stated QS adjustments: QV's nearest mortice-lock row and closer row are a grade above the specified Grade 2 / EN3 product (-30% and -60% applied to the published AKL rates at the low end; high end = QV as published), and by the unresolved question of whether QV's Hardware-section rows include fixing. For comparison, the scenario's own $620–880/leaf is roughly 40% below this low end and is only reachable with value-brand Grade 2 and economy EN3 hardware, which QV does not price. Re-run the closer and lockset against a supplier quote before using either end of this band.

band.unit: ea (per door leaf, one complete hardware set fitted)
band.basis: Sum of the components above, per leaf, GST exclusive, Auckland 2026, no preliminaries, margin or design fees. Supply of a complete commercial mortice lock set (QV AKL 830–890, corroborated by the importer's 2025 kit list at 745.00 for the equivalent Legge 991 kit), restricted-keying per door (35–95, fetched), 3 registered keys (30–60, fetched), overhead adjustable closer (QV AKL 800–980), 3 SS butt hinges (QV 117.60–176.40), door stop (QV 20.50–51.00), fitting labour (QV carpenter rate 81.30/hr × 1.5–2.0 h = 121.95–162.60) and a 10–30 sundries/set-up allowance. Allowances are about 1% of the band, so the band is carried by cited rates, not by judgement. Mid-point ~$2,205/leaf; for the 25-leaf nominal run, ~$49,100–$61,100. Principal sensitivities: (a) QV prices only LCN closers at 800–1,140, so if a spec-equivalent Briton 1120 (importer list 275.00) is accepted the band drops to roughly $1,350–$1,650/leaf; (b) if the QV hardware rates already include fixing, deduct 122–163; (c) if furniture is not in the QV lock rate, add 270–330. QV hardware rows are unreviewed and do not state finish or inclusions, hence confidence low.

band.unit: ea (one complete hardware set fitted to one door leaf)
band.basis: Sum of the seven components above (low sum 1390.88, high sum 2130.30, mid-point about $1,761/leaf), all NZD and GST exclusive, Auckland 2026, no preliminaries, margin, design or consent. For the nominal 25 leaves on one floor and one visit: about $34,800-$53,300 (mid ~$44,000). Every component is priced off a cited QV CostBuilder row or a fetched supplier page; there are no pure judgement allowances. Confidence is LOW because (a) the closer is a premium LCN row cut by 50% to reach the specified standard-range EN 1154 size 3 unit, (b) QV's lock, closer and door-stop rates do not state whether fixing is included and I have assumed it is (the reverse assumption adds about $75-$160/leaf), and (c) the keying and key-cutting figures are a locksmith's indicative ranges rather than quotes. Two structural points: the non-per-leaf items (master-key system set-up and site set-up/handover) are small and amortise to a few dollars per leaf over 25 leaves, so the rate is insensitive to run length; and a fire-rated leaf, panic hardware or access control are outside this scope and priced separately.

band.unit: NZD per door leaf (one complete hardware set fitted), excl. GST, Auckland 2026
band.basis: Sum of distinct components only: QV mortice lockset complete $830-$1,040 + QV LCN adjustable closer $800 + QV SS hinges 3 no. supply-only $117.60-$164.64 + QV door stop $20.50-$51 + fetched LockSmart restricted-keying range $35-$95 + QV carpenter 1.0-2.5 h $81.30-$203.25 = $1,884-$2,354 per leaf; nominal 25 leaves = $47,100-$58,850. No aggregate or elemental row used, and hinge/door-stop fixing is added once, in the labour line, because those QV groups are labelled supply only. Confidence is LOW, not medium, for three stated reasons: (1) QV does not disclose whether the unlabelled Hardware groups include fixing, so up to ~$120/leaf could be on the wrong side of the line; (2) the lockset and closer proxies are premium architectural rows (non-stated grade/backset/finish; aluminium-finish LCN closer used for an SSS-spec closer) used in place of the mid-market items actually specified, so the true figure could sit below the low end if value-brand hardware is acceptable; (3) the keying line rests on one locksmith's published range rather than a per-cylinder trade price. Allowances are a small share of the total (only the judgement hours), so the band is established — but it is a cost-plan band for a brand-specified schedule, not a certified price.
